medium_value.description: Align the primary estimand with the per-dollar question: either make the paired difference in confirmed defects per USD primary, enforce equal realized spending, or explicitly limit the primary claim to recall under approximately matched budgets.

Define how the clipped design-effect simulation realizes the target MDE, report the achieved population recall difference after clipping, and calibrate operating characteristics at that achieved difference.
Specify the complete input and tool-access contract for every arm, including repository context, runnable code, network policy, token limits, and prompt contents; explain what 'mount none' permits.
Freeze the isolation protocol between smoke runs, trials, matched sessions, and arms, including fresh conversation state, writable directories, caches, generated files, and execution order.

Specify how findings become distinct predicted defects before computing precision, including duplicate citations, multiple citations for one defect, one citation near multiple anchors, and findings without usable citations.

Add a behavior-aware primary scoring check, or explicitly label the primary metric as anchor-proximity detection and preregister a minimum judge-confirmation threshold for substantive defect-catching claims.

Define the judge sampling algorithm and estimator for overlapping citation-defect pairs and stray regions, including region boundaries, deduplication, allocation when the minimum sample is infeasible, and propagation of sampling uncertainty.
For judge-confirmed stray defects, freeze a common augmented defect key and rescore every arm against it. Specify how unsampled strays and discovery-dependent inclusion are handled.

Complete the positive-control outcome table for zero effect, no eligible pairs, partial exposure, and insufficient valid pairs; identify the exact pairs and trials used for the closed-recall headroom exclusion.

Define the exact-dollar trimming algorithm, including whether sessions can be fractionally included, treatment when the first session exceeds the budget, whether invalid-session costs consume the budget, and handling of unused dollars.
Specify every cost-per-extra-defect case, including zero or negative incremental catches and zero or negative incremental cost, and distinguish these cases from a finite positive ratio.

Specify which matched sessions contribute detections and costs when a cell passes validity with only half its sessions valid. Explicitly exclude contaminated-session detections from the primary union and retain their spend in the relevant cost accounting.

Reconcile the binding cap with the USD 90 overshoot allowance and 'halt only on spend above the cap' rule. State whether USD 3,800 limits reservations or actual expenditure, and define the outcome when the next run cannot be reserved.
Freeze arm execution order and reserve enough budget for complete primary pairs before secondary arms, positive controls, and discretionary reruns can consume the remaining allocation.
Identify the exact immutable commit used as the registration pin and resolve how a file in that commit can bind its own commit identifier without a circular dependency.

Separate byte-identical recomputation of frozen results from fresh model execution. State which artifacts are replayed, which model calls are repeated, and what variation or tolerance is permitted for reruns.

Replace the stopping outcomes with an executable, mutually exclusive decision table, including precedence for both boundaries crossing and the case where only the YES boundary crosses but the interval lies entirely below the MDE.

Define the exact sequential boundary calculation: spending functions, tail allocation, conversion between t and normal scales, which SE enters each statistic, and whether the finite-cluster correction applies to stopping as well as intervals.
Specify how information fractions are bounded and made nondecreasing, including behavior when observed SE increases, becomes zero, or implies an information fraction above one.

Define look timing after exclusions and budget stops: whether looks occur at scheduled group completion or valid-PR thresholds, whether skipped looks are recovered, and when a partial final group receives a terminal analysis.

Make the placebo-failure fallback executable by specifying the permutation-test threshold, whether it is necessary or sufficient for a decision, its treatment across repeated looks, and its interaction with each stopping outcome.

Construct repeated confidence intervals by inverting the actual sequential testing procedure, or document and validate why the proposed symmetric interval has the claimed repeated coverage under both YES and NO stopping.

Freeze the assumed effect used for conditional power, its calculation under each hypothesis, and the operational policy for continuing after FUTILE. Include that policy in the complete-procedure simulation.

Report simulation uncertainty for power and false-positive estimates, define success separately for YES, NO, and SMALL, and reconcile the 'target power achieved' statement with the failure of the joint 0.80 criterion.

State explicitly which system produced the 'round-1 review' that anchors 153 of the 185 v2 defects (is it the production Loa pipeline, and with which model/prompt version?), and promote the pipeline-independent read (review_driven = false or label_source = incident, at most 32 defects) from a buried secondary to a co-reported read printed beside the primary with its own interval and a pre-stated interpretation rule (e.g., a YES on the full key whose direction does not replicate on the independent subset is reported as 'YES, review-anchored').
Add a sensitivity restricting the key to defects with agreement = agreed (excluding the 36 % adjudicated by the lead), placed first in the §10 order.

Specify what happens to N, the groups and the look schedule when the smoke excludes a PR for failing oracle_closed: whether later PRs shift forward to keep [6, 4, 4], or the group shrinks and the look fires at the reduced count, and how the planned final SE / information fraction is adjusted.

Reconcile the judge sample with its reserve: min(all, 10) over arm × PR × class strata (up to 5 × 14 × 4 = 280 strata) can exceed 2,000 items against a USD 30 judge reserve; either set a total cap with proportional down-sampling recorded in key.json or raise the reserve.

In the placebo fallback, give the PR-level permutation test explicit precedence (or require agreement) for the final decision when the Phase 1 placebo fails, and require permutation corroboration for any interim decision at the 6-PR look.
Pre-specify estimation of within-PR session correlation ρ from the Phase 1 matched cells' per-defect detection vectors, and report the implied design effect and re-simulated power beside the primary.

Bind the v2 key file(s) explicitly in REGISTRATION.json (path and sha256 of the label manifest, codebook and adjudication rules DEC-0717/0719), not only via the suite MANIFEST.sha256 and the result.md path.

State that the 23 rows behind ĉ_full include the codex dissent cost under the same budget_scale: diff / max 600 c configuration, and that the 23 ĉ_bare rows were run with Opus 5.5 --effort high; otherwise re-fit on the matching subset.

State pr-15's share of the defect-weighted primary (45 / 185 = 24 %) in §2 and pre-commit to printing the leave-pr-15-out read beside the primary, and add a logit-scale (odds-ratio) Δ as a secondary estimand.
State that pairs are formed by trial index (full trial i with matched trial i) and either justify it or pool all valid cells per arm within a PR instead of excluding a pair when one cell fails.
Define the denominator of the 25 % guard (cells, pairs or sessions, per arm) and whether smoke and open-mount rows count.

List the PRs and arms covered by the 63 existing runs used for the cost fits, power profiles and Phase 0 placebo, and reconcile '4 excluded PRs supply the power profiles' (§2) with '6 PR profiles' (§7) and '21 pairs over 6 PRs' (§8). Confirm in the text that pr-11, pr-14, pr-15 and pr-16 (which carry cycle-131 labels) never had an a1_* run.
Replace the 10,000-draw Monte Carlo PR-level permutation with exact enumeration of all 2^P arm assignments (≤ 16,384 at P = 14).
Note in limitations that the blind annotators and the judge are the same model as the bare comparator (Opus 5.5), or use a different model for the judge.

Document how the single seed 20261021 is split into independent RNG streams for corpus order, bootstrap, permutation, placebo shuffles, power simulation and judge sampling (e.g., named sub-seeds derived by hashing).
State that the matched union is taken over valid sessions only, and pre-specify per-session precision (not union precision) as the precision metric comparable to the full arm.

Specify where the 'FUTILE (non-binding)' continuation decision is recorded before the next group runs, and that the lead's choice to continue is logged in NOTES.md with the conditional-power values at that look.

Pre-specify a tolerance on the smoke's realized full/bare cost ratio (e.g., median realized ratio outside 0.75–1.33 × predicted) that triggers a REGISTRATION-2 re-derivation of k before any G1 row, and a threshold on the share of dollar-flagged pairs (e.g., > 25 %) above which the exact-dollar trim replaces the raw matched union as the headline primary.

Give the positive control its own cluster-t interval and a minimum PR count (e.g., ≥ 3 G1 PRs with headroom) below which it is 'not exercised'; make 'void' depend on the interval's upper bound being < 0 (or excluding the expected +0.07), not on the sign of the point estimate; and state that the control is evaluated before the G1 look so no YES/NO can be issued on a void study.

Add rules for the information fraction: clip t_k to min(t_k, 1 − ε) at interim looks when the bootstrap SE comes in below the planned final SE, force t = 1 (spend all remaining α) at whatever look is declared final — including a final look at fewer than 14 PRs after a spend stop or smoke exclusion — and state that df = P − 1 uses the realized P at that look.

Name the interval used in the YES condition ('not entirely below the MDE') — use the repeated confidence interval Δ̂ ± b_k·SE so that YES/NO/SMALL are mutually exhaustive — and define the conditional-power computation for FUTILE (assumed effect: current estimate, MDE, or both) and whether the power simulation treated FUTILE as a stop.

Change '§5 target power 0.80 (achieved: §7)' to state the achieved values (P(YES | MDE) = 0.82, P(NO | 0) = 0.78) and that the DEC-0713 joint criterion is not met at any N, with the DEC-0718 acceptance referenced.

Justify in §1/§3 why the primary comparator is a different model (Opus 5.5 bare) rather than the same-model bare arm (Fable 5.1), state how the two contrasts are to be interpreted jointly (pipeline-plus-model vs pipeline-only value-add), and report the standard errors of the 6-row ĉ_bare_fable fit with a k′ ± 1 sensitivity for the same-model contrast.
Add an exposure column for the dissent model (gpt-5.5-pro/codex) to the corpus table and include its sessions in the per-run contamination scan and oracle check.

Pre-specify a memorization sensitivity for the unverified Opus 5.5 exposure: e.g., a blind probe asking the bare model to reproduce each fix hunk from head context (scored by the same pm3 rule), or a split of the primary by label_source (fix-commit-only vs incident) with the direction stated in advance.

blockers.concern: Knowledge-cutoff dates and runtime oracle scans do not establish that a model has never encountered the public fixes, and Opus exposure is explicitly unverified.
blockers.why_matters: Differential memorization can affect the cross-model primary comparison without generating detectable runtime contamination.
blockers.recommendation: Separate runtime leakage from prior model exposure, document model release and repository-publication timelines, and qualify the unseen-PR claim or use private prospective fixtures.

blockers.concern: Pairwise exclusion conditions analysis on successful outcomes from both arms, while matched cells can remain valid after losing nearly half their sessions.
blockers.why_matters: Difficulty-dependent failures can select an easier subset and produce unequal effective budgets. Bounds on excluded matched sessions do not cover missing full cells or excluded PR pairs.
blockers.recommendation: Add an all-assigned-pairs operational analysis counting failures and all spend, plus bounds for missing cells and entire excluded pairs in both arms.

blockers.concern: Primary credit depends on a citation falling within three lines of an anchor, without a stated requirement that the finding describe the corresponding wrong behavior.
blockers.why_matters: An unrelated finding near an anchor can receive credit, while a correct finding citing a caller or another affected site can miss. Citation style and volume can change the apparent treatment effect.
blockers.recommendation: Require semantic agreement with the defect for primary credit, and audit duplicate credit, incidental proximity, and correct findings outside the citation window.

blockers.concern: The PR-level permutation test assumes exchangeability of structurally different arms without randomized treatment assignment or an argument establishing exchangeability under the tested null.
blockers.why_matters: Equal average recall does not imply interchangeable arm distributions, especially with different models, session counts, and failure processes.
blockers.recommendation: State the stronger null required by the test and validate its size under unequal variances and arm-specific failures; specify how permutation evidence enters the sequential decision.

blockers.concern: The defect key is largely defined by the pipeline under test. 153 of 185 defects (83 %) are review-driven, i.e. the round-1 review of that very PR cited the site and the fix followed; four fixtures (pr-28, pr-14, pr-25, pr-11) are 100 % review-driven. The full arm re-running the same pipeline on the same input is being graded against a subset of real defects selected for being pipeline-findable. The pipeline-independent read has at most 32 defects and cannot detect a 0.10 MDE.
blockers.why_matters: Δ is biased upward by construction regardless of how real each labelled defect is; a YES on the full key may mean 'the pipeline re-finds what it previously found', which the title 'conclusive review-catch answer' would overstate.
blockers.location: §1 Confirmed defect / review_driven; §2 table review-driven column; §5 secondary pipeline-independent read
blockers.recommendation: Pre-register that a YES is reported as conditional on the sign of the pipeline-independent read; report recall per arm stratified by label_source and review_driven at every look; state the expected direction of bias in §1; consider weighting the primary so review-driven and independent defects contribute equally.

blockers.concern: The outcome space mislabels significant harm. If Δ̂ is significantly negative, the two-sided z_yes crosses but the interval is entirely below the MDE (not YES); z_no crosses but z_yes has crossed (not NO); both crossed → the outcome is 'SMALL'. There is no HARM/WORSE outcome.
blockers.why_matters: A pipeline that is significantly worse than the bare model at equal dollars would be headlined as a small effect; the hashed rule cannot be corrected without an amendment.
blockers.recommendation: Add a WORSE outcome (z_yes crosses with Δ̂ < 0) and restrict SMALL to Δ̂ ≥ 0 with both boundaries crossed; or make the YES test one-sided and define NO/SMALL accordingly.

blockers.concern: The placebo already fails its calibration criterion, but the fallback relies on a sequential procedure calibrated under a particular fitted simulation and a permutation test whose validity is assumed.
blockers.why_matters: Neither fallback establishes reliable error control for the actual corpus when the primary interval is known to fail a planned diagnostic.
blockers.recommendation: Validate the complete fallback decision procedure under multiple plausible null-generating mechanisms, including heterogeneous effects, correlated sessions, missingness, and the observed cluster sizes.

blockers.concern: The positive-control void rule rests on the sign of a noisy point estimate. The control runs on G1 only (≤ 6 PRs, 2 trials), then excludes any PR whose closed-mount recall exceeds 0.9, which with expected full-arm recall 0.86 may leave 2–4 PRs. The expected effect is only +0.07. A negative estimate with oracle exposure declares every other read void. Under a true +0.07 the chance of a negative sign on 2–4 clusters is plausibly 10–25 %; under a true zero effect the control 'passes' half the time, so it neither reliably protects nor reliably fails.
blockers.why_matters: A USD 3,800 study can be voided by sampling noise in a sub-experiment with no stated power, and the rule is in the hashed text so it cannot be softened afterwards without an amendment that must report both reads.
blockers.recommendation: Before hashing: simulate P(void | true +0.07) and P(pass | 0) for the control as designed and record both; replace the bare sign test with a pre-specified one-sided interval or a minimum number of exposed PRs; run the control across all groups rather than G1 alone; and downgrade the consequence from 'void' to 'reads reported as unconfirmed' unless the estimate is significantly negative.

blockers.concern: The power model is fitted to six historical PR profiles under an earlier label set, and the registered sensitivity scenarios reduce power substantially below the target.
blockers.why_matters: The advertised 0.82 power is fragile to plausible session correlation and may not transfer to the new corpus or v2 labels.
blockers.recommendation: Report Monte Carlo uncertainty, achieved rather than nominal effect sizes after clipping, and decision error rates across the sensitivity scenarios; describe the study as potentially inconclusive.

blockers.concern: The primary estimand measures recall, while the stated question asks for confirmed defects per dollar. Realized cost mismatches are only flagged, and pairs outside the 25% tolerance remain in the primary analysis.
blockers.why_matters: A YES could reflect greater expenditure rather than greater cost effectiveness.
blockers.recommendation: Make a cost effectiveness contrast primary, or require realized budget equivalence for the primary comparison and specify treatment of unmatched pairs.

blockers.concern: The reference labels remain strongly tied to historical review and subsequent fixes: 153 of 185 defects are review-driven, and unreported or unfixed defects are generally absent.
blockers.why_matters: The benchmark can favor a pipeline resembling the process that generated the labels and penalize valid discoveries outside that process. Blind annotation does not remove this selection bias.
blockers.recommendation: Add an independent head-code audit and adjudicate novel findings symmetrically across arms; restrict conclusions explicitly to the frozen known-defect set until that work is complete.

blockers.concern: The sequential rule does not fully specify how information fractions and looks behave with exclusions or a budget-truncated group. Nominal looks require 6, 10, and 14 valid PRs, although excluded PRs are not replaced.
blockers.why_matters: Later looks may never be reached, and ad hoc partial-group looks can invalidate spending calculations.
blockers.recommendation: Define looks by completed scheduled groups, exact rules for partial groups and unattainable valid-PR counts, and handling of nonmonotone or greater-than-one information fractions.

blockers.concern: The stopping categories are not mutually exclusive as written: when both statistics cross and the interval condition holds, both YES and SMALL apply.
blockers.why_matters: Outcome classification can depend on implementation order, undermining the registered decision rule.
blockers.recommendation: Specify an ordered, exhaustive decision table, including signed crossing rules, the meaning of the interval condition, and final-look CONTINUE.

The review_driven flag exists but nothing in the decision rule uses it, and the independent subset is too small to carry weight unless its role is fixed in advance.","location":"\u00a71 Question and construct (v2 label set, review_driven); \u00a75 Secondary (pipeline-independent read)","priority":"HIGH","confidence":0.8},{"id":"IMP-002","description":"List the PRs and arms covered by the 63 existing runs used for the cost fits, power profiles and Phase 0 placebo, and reconcile '4 excluded PRs supply the power profiles' (\u00a72) with '6 PR profiles' (\u00a77) and '21 pairs over 6 PRs' (\u00a78). An amendment path exists (\u00a712) but no rule says when to use it, so the choice would be made post hoc.","location":"\u00a73 k derivation; \u00a74 Dollar matching; \u00a711 Smoke; \u00a712 Amendments","priority":"HIGH","confidence":0.75},{"id":"IMP-004","description":"Give the positive control its own cluster-t interval and a minimum PR count (e.g., \u2265 3 G1 PRs with headroom) below which it is 'not exercised'; make 'void' depend on the interval's upper bound being < 0 (or excluding the expected +0.07), not on the sign of the point estimate; and state that the control is evaluated before the G1 look so no YES/NO can be issued on a void study.","rationale":"With an expected effect of +0.07 and at most 6 PRs (fewer after the >0.9 recall exclusion, which pr-28 and pr-25 with 3\u20134 defects will likely hit), a negative point estimate by chance alone is plausible (~5\u201310 %), and the current rule voids every other read on that noise. The ordering relative to the first look is unspecified.","location":"\u00a78 Positive control; \u00a76 Looks after G1","priority":"HIGH","confidence":0.75},{"id":"IMP-005","description":"Add rules for the information fraction: clip t_k to min(t_k, 1 \u2212 \u03b5) at interim looks when the bootstrap SE comes in below the planned final SE, force t = 1 (spend all remaining \u03b1) at whatever look is declared final \u2014 including a final look at fewer than 14 PRs after a spend stop or smoke exclusion \u2014 and state that df = P \u2212 1 uses the realized P at that look.","rationale":"t_k = SE\u00b2_planned/SE\u00b2_k is estimated from a noisy 6- or 10-cluster bootstrap and can exceed 1 before the last look, where the Lan\u2013DeMets spending function is undefined; without a final-look override, a truncated study would never spend its full \u03b1 and the calibrated P(YES | 0) = 0.034 no longer applies.","location":"\u00a76 Stopping rule (information fraction, boundaries); \u00a77 partial group","priority":"HIGH","confidence":0.8},{"id":"IMP-006","description":"Name the interval used in the YES condition ('not entirely below the MDE') \u2014 use the repeated confidence interval \u0394\u0302 \u00b1 b_k\u00b7SE so that YES/NO/SMALL are mutually exhaustive \u2014 and define the conditional-power computation for FUTILE (assumed effect: current estimate, MDE, or both) and whether the power simulation treated FUTILE as a stop.","rationale":"With the naive interval, a look can have z_yes crossing, the naive upper bound below the MDE, and z_no not crossing, which maps to none of YES/NO/SMALL and is reported as 'inconclusive' despite a significant positive effect.
